title: A project's airgap settings (testing/airgap.yaml)
description: What the airgap agent allows in one project, beyond the machine itself: the stand-ins its tests reach, the folders they write in, and how it treats production profiles. Words follow GLOSSARY.md.

mode.description: refuse: stop every call not allowed (the default). report: let every call go ahead, and record it. off: neither.

target.description: host:port (localhost:8089), a host on its own, a JDBC or HTTP URL prefix, process:name for a program (its file name or full path), or native:name for a native library; programs and libraries exactly, or with * for any run of characters.

reason.description: What the stand-in is, for example "WireMock standing in for the postcode service".

packages.description: Package prefixes of the project's own code, such as com.example., so the report names the project's line that made each call, not a library's. The agent's project setting adds to them.

production_profiles.description: Spring profile names that mean production. A run with any of them active stops at once.

file_writes.description: Whether writes, deletes, renames and new folders outside the project are only reported (the default) or, when the mode is refuse, refused. Inside the project means the build's root folder, the temporary folder, the report's folder and write_folders.

write_folders.description: Folders outside the build's root that the tests may write in, as if they were the project's.

folder.description: The folder: absolute, relative to the build's root folder, or under the home folder with ~/ (~/.m2/repository).

reason.description: Why the tests write there, for example "the tests install the library they build".
